1.title: Digital Product and Service Management: Key Concepts
1.text: Welcome to Module one: Digital Product and Service Management: Key Concepts. It covers the exam area Key eye til terms and definitions. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Define digital product and service management, product, service, digital product, digital service, good, continual improvement, the lifecycle, utility, warranty, user experience and sustainability. Explain service offerings, service interactions, service actions, transfer of goods and access to resources. Know the benefits of eye til. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Key eye til terms and definitions (thirty percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: The big idea
1.text: The big idea. eye til is a framework of best practice for digital product and service management: how an organization creates, delivers and continually improves products and services so that value is co-created with the people who use them. eye til four spoke of I T service management and only services. Version five treats products and services as two sides of the same digital solution.

1.title: The big idea, continued
1.text: The big idea. The figure shows this: Key concepts map: product, service, digital, good, offering.

1.title: Product, service and good
1.text: Product, service and good. Digital product and service management. Managing digital products and services across their whole life so they create value. Product. A configuration of resources (people, processes, technology, information) designed to offer value to a consumer. Service. A means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating the outcomes consumers want, without the consumer managing the specific costs and risks. Digital product. A product that depends on digital technology. Digital service. A service that is enabled by digital technology. Good. An item whose ownership is transferred to the consumer. Exam tip: Product equals the configuration of resources. Service equals the way value is co-created, with the provider carrying the costs and risks. A product can be offered as a service.

1.title: Product, service and good, continued
1.text: Product, service and good. Continual improvement is the recurring activity of improving products, services, practices and the whole eye til Value System. The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle is the model of eight activities (discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support) that apply to every product and service (Modules five to seven).

1.title: Service offerings
1.text: Service offerings. Service offering. A formal description of one or more services designed to meet the needs of a target consumer group. Service interactions. The exchanges between the provider and the consumer while the service is used. Service actions. Actions the provider performs for the consumer, such as running a process. Transfer of goods. Ownership of a good passes to the consumer. Access to resources. The consumer may use a resource (a licence, a subscription) but the provider keeps ownership.

1.title: Service offerings, continued
1.text: Service offerings. An offering can combine goods, access to resources and service actions. Example: a laptop bought outright is a transfer of goods; a cloud tool used by subscription is access to resources; the help desk fixing a fault is a service action. Exam tip: Owns it afterward equals transfer of goods. Uses it but does not own it equals access to resources. Someone does work for you equals service action.

1.title: Utility, warranty, user experience, sustainability
1.text: Utility, warranty, user experience, sustainability. Utility. Is it fit for purpose? (does what is needed). Warranty. Is it fit for use? (available, secure, reliable, enough capacity). User experience. How does using it feel to the people involved? Sustainability. Can it continue without harming people, the environment or the organization over time? These four, with outcomes, costs and risks, are the areas of value (Module two).

1.title: Benefits of ITIL
1.text: Benefits of eye til. Enterprises. A common language, better value from digital investment, better alignment with business goals. Managed service providers. Clearer service offerings, better relationships, repeatable good practice. Digital product vendors. Guidance to build, run and support products so customers get value. Digital product and service management professionals. Recognized skills, a shared vocabulary, a path to higher eye til qualifications. Exam tip: In a List question, check each statement on its own: "fit for purpose" is utility, "fit for use" is warranty. Swapping them is the classic trap.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Contoso Retail buys a point-of-sale tablet and now owns it. Which concept does this describe? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Transfer of goods. Ownership passes to the consumer, so it is a transfer of goods.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company pays a monthly fee to use a cloud file-sharing tool that the vendor keeps owning and running. Which concept applies? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Access to resources. The consumer may use the resource while the provider keeps ownership.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statement about utility and warranty is C O R R E C T? (one) Utility means the product is fit for purpose. (two) Utility means the product is fit for use. (three) Warranty means the product is fit for use. (four) Warranty means the product is fit for purpose. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one and three. Utility is fit for purpose and warranty is fit for use.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). A blank is a formal description of one or more services designed to address the needs of a target consumer group. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Service offering. That is the definition of a service offering.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. The help desk resets a user's locked account. Which concept is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A service action. The provider performs an action for the consumer.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What describes a service, as eye til defines it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A means of enabling value co-creation while the provider carries specific costs and risks. A service enables co-created value without the consumer managing those costs and risks.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define a product. Answer: A configuration of an organization's resources designed to offer value to a consumer. Question two. What question does utility answer? Answer: Is it fit for purpose? Question three. What question does warranty answer? Answer: Is it fit for use?

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a good? Answer: An item whose ownership is transferred to the consumer. Question five. Name the three things a service offering can combine. Answer: Goods, access to resources and service actions. Question six. What are the eight lifecycle activities? Answer: Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver and support.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Product or service: resources configured to offer value or enabling co-creation, provider carries costs and risks. Good: ownership is transferred. Offering: goods plus access to resources plus service actions. Utility or warranty: fit for purpose or fit for use. Also: user experience and sustainability are areas of value.
